clue.text: Plato, for example, gave valid answer to a medical man

parts.note: to meet a demand or objection is to answer it satisfactorily, so this gives met
a doctor of medicine is a physician

explanation.surface: Someone gave a doctor a sound reply, with Plato cited as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: Plato is the example of a philosopher of first principles, beyond physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was a philosopher concerned with being and reality, the field of metaphysics, so he is an example of such a thinker.

clue.text: Evoked by Dr Faustus? The devil he is!

definitions.text: Evoked by Dr Faustus? The devil he is!

parts.words: Evoked by Dr Faustus? The devil he is!
parts.note: Marlowe's Doctor Faustus conjures up a demon who becomes his servant; the exclamation confirms the figure summoned is a devil

explanation.definitionFit: In Marlowe's play the demon Faustus calls up, and sells his soul to, is a devil of the underworld.

clue.text: Expression of impatience ' it upset all the musicians

parts.note: tut is the click of the tongue people make when impatient

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word it is turned upside down, read bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone tuts impatiently and knocks something over, annoying the whole band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IT into TI, which follows TUT.
explanation.definitionFit: In a score, the marking tells every player of the orchestra to play together, as opposed to a soloist.

clue.text: How the weary ploughman returns home?

definitions.text: How the weary ploughman returns home?

parts.words: How the weary ploughman returns home?
parts.note: echoes Gray's Elegy, where the ploughman homeward plods his weary way, so the manner of his going is slow and heavy-footed

explanation.definitionFit: Walking with slow, heavy, tired steps is the manner of a tired farm worker trudging back at dusk.

clue.text: Old warrior king is captured in overthrow of Troy

indicators.note: the king and the word is are taken prisoner inside the other piece, so they sit within it
an overthrow turns something over, so the word Troy is read backwards

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king is taken prisoner when the city of Troy falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrow of' turns TROY into YORT; 'captured in' puts K and IS inside it, between YOR and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the House of York fought in the Wars of the Roses, so is a soldier of the past.

clue.text: Ape roaming about at one time

indicators.note: wandering about suggests the letters of at, one and time move around into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An ape is wandering around at some point in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roaming about' rearranges AT + I + TIME into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy their behaviour, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Small amount identified by a character in Aeschylus

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a tiny quantity, and the Greek letter i, which appears in the Greek spelling of the playwright's name.

clue.text: Recent dash to produce a paper on this

parts.note: something recent is new
a dash is a short fast run, a sprint

explanation.surface: A reporter makes a quick dash to get the latest story into the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap rough paper is the stock that daily papers are printed on.

clue.text: Dine out after exploit her supporter found frivolous

indicators.note: the rearranged dine letters come after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: an exploit is a deed of daring, a feat
taken as written
a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: dine out tells us to put the letters of dine out of their order

explanation.surface: After a heroic deed, she and her boyfriend go out to dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DINE into INED, placed 'after' FEAT + HER + BRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone silly and scatterbrained is said to have a head stuffed with down.

clue.text: Dried petals from plant for French King Emperor

parts.note: to pot a plant is to plant it in a pot
pour is French for for
R is from Rex, Latin for king
I is from Imperator, Latin for emperor, as in coins marked R I

explanation.surface: Flowers are dried for the King Emperor of France.
explanation.walkthrough: R I, Rex Imperator, appeared on coins of British kings who were also emperors of India.
explanation.definitionFit: A scented bowl mixture is made of dried flower heads and spices.

clue.text: Article in. Wild West used by beater

indicators.note: the article is set inside the other letters
wild means the letters of west run riot into a new order

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about the Wild West features a hunting beater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges WEST into TWSE; 'in' puts A after the T. A tawse is a leather strap once used to beat schoolchildren in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish leather strap was used by teachers to punish pupils, an implement that beats.

clue.text: Island parliamentarians rejected this literary work

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for parliamentarians is read backwards

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: Island politicians throw out a famous book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns DAIL into LIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem of the Trojan War is a celebrated piece of literature.

clue.text: Muslim potentate's claim to be without one parent?

parts.note: someone claiming to be something says I'm a

indicators.note: without means the letter for one is left out

parts.note: ma is a mother
a means one

explanation.surface: A Muslim ruler wonders if he is missing a mother.
explanation.walkthrough: I'M A + MA is the claim to be a parent; 'without' drops one A.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is used for some Muslim rulers and leaders of prayer, so a ruler in Islam.

clue.text: Small quantity to look out for and note

definitions.text: to look out for and note

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a little bit of something, and the verb meaning to notice or catch sight of.

clue.text: Guffaw distressed her also? How disgusting!

indicators.note: distressed suggests the letters of her and also are thrown into disorder

parts.note: ugh is the exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone guffaws, upsetting a woman who finds it repulsive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' rearranges HER + ALSO into HORSELA.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud coarse laugh is a guffaw, synonym.

clue.text: The chief difficulty, a mass of hair

parts.note: the chief is the top
a knot is a tangled difficulty

explanation.surface: The main problem is a tangle of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuft of hair tied on the crown of the head is a gathered bunch.

clue.text: Serving the people -a new style for former tax-collectors

parts.note: the public is the people
NS is the abbreviation for New Style, the Gregorian calendar

explanation.surface: Serving the public in a new way, like collectors of taxes once did.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible the tax-gatherers of Roman times are called by this name, the 'publicans and sinners'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman times the men who farmed taxes were given this name, used in the Gospels.

clue.text: Elgar's first melodic figure arousing strong feeling

indicators.note: Elgar's first means the first letter of the composer's name

parts.note: a motive is a recurring musical figure, a motif

explanation.surface: Elgar's first musical theme is deeply stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stirs the emotions provokes intense feeling.

clue.text: Nourishment for Hassan hidden in fruit-tree?

indicators.note: hidden in tells us one piece is put inside the fruit tree

parts.note: a plum is a fruit tree
Abu goes before Hassan, as in Weber's opera Abu Hassan

explanation.surface: Food for a man called Hassan is tucked away in an orchard tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden in' puts ABU inside PLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare word means food or nutriment, also bland intellectual fare.

clue.text: Thursday started misty. Tiny kid worried about it

indicators.note: started misty means the first letter of misty
the rearranged kid goes around the word for tiny
worried suggests the letters of kid are shaken up

parts.note: wee is Scottish for tiny

explanation.surface: A misty start to Thursday upsets a little child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges KID into IDK, and 'about' puts it round WEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thursday falls around the centre of the working week.

clue.text: Shaw's dramatic treatment to save rejected copper

indicators.note: a dramatic treatment reworks the playwright's name, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for save is read backwards

parts.note: save means except, but

explanation.surface: A playwright's dramatic handling of a policeman left out of the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dramatic treatment' rearranges SHAW into WASH; 'rejected' turns BUT into TUB. A copper is a large metal tub for boiling laundry in old British homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A large metal vessel for boiling laundry was called a copper in old households.

clue.text: Strike endlessly, supported by a French-speaker in Belgium

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word for strike is removed

parts.note: to wallop is to strike hard
in a down clue, a piece above on stands supported by it

explanation.surface: Someone keeps hitting a French-speaking Belgian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the P of WALLOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Walloon people of southern Belgium speak a French dialect.

clue.text: Give out in semitropical heat

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the word semitropical

explanation.surface: Something radiates warmth in the heat of the semitropics.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge, a synonym of give out.

clue.text: Superstar resting, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the word for resting is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: someone resting is idle

explanation.surface: Is a famous star simply taking a break?
explanation.walkthrough: An out-of-work actor is said to be 'resting'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hugely admired celebrity is worshipped by fans.

clue.text: Creature left a mark in a Californian city

indicators.note: a and the mark go inside the city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, a city in California
M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: An animal left a mark in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A + M inside LA.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American woolly pack animal is an animal.

clue.text: A mix-up about love in principle

indicators.note: the mixed-up letters go around the letter for love
mix-up tells us the letters of a and mix are jumbled

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A confusion about love, in principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' rearranges A + MIX into AXIM, and 'about' puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident truth taken as a starting point is a principle.

clue.text: Soldier died in desert

indicators.note: the word for died goes inside the word for soldier

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
OB is short for obiit, Latin for died

explanation.surface: A soldier perished in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OB inside GI.
explanation.definitionFit: The great desert of Mongolia and northern China is a named desert.

clue.text: Muse for a long time about Holy Writ

parts.note: an era is a long period

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters for Holy Writ are read backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone has long reflected on Scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns OT into TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: No I clue to reforming the art of .speaking

indicators.note: reforming means shaping again, so the letters of no, I, clue and to are rearranged

explanation.surface: No crossword hint will reform a mumbler's diction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforming' rearranges NO I CLUE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Elocution is the skill of clear and expressive diction.

clue.text: Colonel Blimp's staff bogged down?

parts.note: a staff is a walking stick
something bogged down is stuck fast, as if in the mud

explanation.surface: The old colonel's walking cane is stuck in a bog.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp is a British cartoon figure of a pompous, reactionary old officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon colonel is a byword for a hidebound conservative who resists change.
